thread.title: Samsung: What Reviewers Are Saying About the New Galaxy Note 9

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Samsung: What Reviewers Are Saying About the New Galaxy Note 9
text:
Photo: Samsung By David Marino-Nachison Aug. 20, 2018 7:00 a.m. ET The Galaxy Note 9 , Samsung’s latest “phablet”—or, if you prefer, phone with a really big screen—is the latest entry in the four-digit phone price roundup. But is it worth all that dough?
After reading a number of reviews, the answer seems to be a general “yes.” That’s not to say that they describe the phone as something that screams “Must Buy At Any Price,” but rather that if this is a price point you’d consider, this phone deserves its place in the conversation.
As to more hands-on impressions: At Wired, Lauren Goode’s review summed up the tone of what many others seemed to think.
Samsung's newest phone has more features, options and possibilities than the rest. WSJ's David Pierce reviews this big, fast, funky phone made for power users. Photo/Video: Emily Prapuolenis/The Wall Street Journal “It’s super fast, comes with more storage than even obsessive photo takers or game players might know what to do with, and its S Pen stylus now doubles as a remote control,” she wrote. “Samsung has somehow found ways to differentiate this phone from the Galaxy S9, it’s other flagship phone . It has justified the bigness.”
• The point of a big phone is a big screen, and the Note 9’s delivers, according to CNBC’s Todd Haselton .
“I love the 6.4-inch display paired with the new stereo speakers, the latter of which haven’t appeared on a Galaxy Note before,” he wrote. “This is a phone for someone who loves to watch movies, TV shows and play games, since they all make the most of the massive screen.”
• Adam Ismail, writing for Tom’s Guide , compared the phone to Apple’s (AAPL) iPhone X and Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Google Pixel 2 XL—focusing, as it were, on the cameras. His favorite ended up the Pixel.
“Samsung has once again developed an excellent low-light shooter, and the Note 9 also produced a better-looking flower close-up than the competition,” he wrote. “However, for most other occasions, outdoors or in, the Pixel 2 XL still edges out Samsung’s flagship.”
Newsletter Sign-up • Some reviewers praised the phone’s battery life. Mike Murphy at Quartz gave it mixed reviews, saying he found the meter measuring the remaining power unreliable.
“There were days where the phone worked like a champion (like when I kept the screen on for almost the entirety of a five-hour drive, while the phone was providing directions, and still had over 30% battery left), and days where it seemed like regular use drained it just like any other phone,” he wrote. “But for the most part, the large, 4,000 mAh battery had enough to get me through the day, and recharged quickly.”
• And Popular Science, because it’s 2018, looked at the phone from the perspective of a gamer—a Fortnite player, to be exact. “If you’re seriously into mobile gaming, then the Note 9 has a lot going for it,” Stan Horaczek wrote , praising the battery life, coolness during long play sessions, and display color.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 • If price is no object, read Sam Rutherford’s review for Gizmodo , which calls the phone “a top-to-bottom improvement on how much you can cram in a phone and what it can do.”
“It’s as if on the Note 9, Samsung took the ridiculous excess of a stretch Ferrari limo, added back in the performance that prancing horse logo is supposed to deliver, and then went over everything with the kind of attention normally reserved for overly-tweezed Michelin star meals,” Rutherford wrote.
• But if price is in fact an object, tune in to BGR’s Zach Epstein : Given its price, he wrote, you may want to wait for a next-generation high-end Android phone, even though it’s a high-quality machine.
“Upgrading to the Note 9 now could spoil things if the Galaxy S10 catches your eye in January,” he wrote. “That said, the Galaxy Note 9 is absolutely the best flagship Android phone you can buy right now, all things considered. Other Android phones come close, but no other smartphone can match the Galaxy Note 9’s power, display quality, or overall user experience.”
